 The 1099 deadline is coming: Due dates, requirements, and penalties for filing
 Posted
 Thursday, 
 November 19, 2026 
 8:00 am 
 Kai Des Etages for Intuit QuickBooks 
 Small businesses that paid contractors in 2026 have a short window to get their forms ready before Form 1099-NEC is due Feb. 1, 2027 .
 Filing your tax forms before the 1099 deadline means complying with tax regulations and avoiding penalties. It also ensures the individuals and businesses you work with can meet their tax deadlines.
 What is a 1099  form? It’s a tax form to report various types of income other than wages and salaries.
 The filing deadlines and penalties can vary depending on the 1099 form you send or receive.
 Form 1099-NEC   is due Feb. 1, 2027, to both recipients and the IRS  (shifted from Jan. 31, which falls on a Sunday).
 Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-K  are due to recipients by Feb. 1, 2027, and to the IRS by March 1, 2027 (paper) or March 31, 2027 (e-file).
 Businesses must generally issue a 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC  if they pay $2,000 or more for services, rent, or other reportable income (up from the previous $600 threshold).
 Form 1099-K has a separate threshold:  it applies once payments through third-party platforms exceed $20,000 and 200 transactions  in a calendar year.
 Late or missing 1099s  can trigger penalties of $60-$690 per form , depending on how late they are filed.
 Intuit QuickBooks  looks at some of the common 1099 forms, their due dates, the consequences of missing deadlines, and the process for getting an extension.
 When are 1099s due?
 Meeting the 1099 filing deadline is crucial for small business owners who want to avoid penalties. The IRS requires the timely submission of over 20 different types of 1099 forms .
 Most small businesses, however, only deal with a few, such as Forms 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC, and 1099-K.
 Here are the key deadlines for the 2027 tax season: 
 Form 1099-NEC:  Due Feb. 1, 2027 (to both recipients and the IRS, whether paper or e-file—shifted from Jan. 31, which falls on a Sunday).
 Form 1099-MISC:  Due Feb. 1, 2027, to recipients; file with the IRS by March 1, 2027 (paper, shifted from Feb. 28) or March 31, 2027 (e-file).
 Form 1099-K:  Same deadlines as Form 1099-MISC, though its reporting threshold is different (see below).
 When do you need to issue 1099 forms?
 Misunderstanding what 1099 forms are and how to use them is one of the common mistakes made on 1099s .
 Businesses and individuals who make qualifying payments are responsible for issuing 1099 forms. Recipients must also get a copy for their own tax reporting.
 Threshold:  You must generally issue a 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC if you’ve paid $2,000 or more in a calendar year for services, rent, or other reportable income. Up from the previous $600 threshold.
 1099-NEC:  For contractor or freelancer services.
 1099-MISC:  For rent, legal fees, and certain miscellaneous payments.
 1099-K:  For businesses receiving payments through platforms like PayPal, Venmo, or online marketplaces, once those payments exceed $20,000 and 200 transactions  in a calendar year.
 If you paid $2,000 or more to an individual or unincorporated business for services during 2026, you’ll likely need to issue a 1099 by Feb. 1, 2027.
 For example, if you pay a contractor or a freelancer for services, you would issue a 1099-NEC form to report their nonemployee compensation. However, if you need to report rent or attorney fee payments, you’ll need to file Form 1099-MISC.
 Form 1099-K  is a tax form that small businesses receive if they use an online marketplace like eBay or if they use third-party payment applications such as PayPal.
 And remember that the deadlines for the 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC  forms are different. The 1099-NEC deadline is Feb. 1, 2027, for paper or e-filing with the IRS, while the 1099-MISC deadline is March 1, 2027, for paper filing and March 31, 2027, for e-filing with the IRS.
 The deadline for Form 1099-K is the same as Form 1099-MISC, though its $20,000/200 transaction reporting threshold is separate from the $2,000 threshold that applies to 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC.
 Business owners can accurately report income and expenses and avoid penalties by keeping track of the key Form 1099 due dates and ensuring timely filing.
 Form 1099 late filing penalty
 Failing to meet the deadlines for filing Form 1099 can result in penalties and fees. The penalties for missing these deadlines can vary depending on the timing of the filing—and how late it is.
 The Form 1099 late filing penalty  is as follows, based on how late you file:
 $60 per form if you file within 30 days after the due date
 $130 per form if over 30 days late but before Aug. 2
 $340 per form after Aug. 1, or if you don’t file at all
 $690 per form for intentionally disregarding filing requirements
 To avoid these penalties, file on time.
 Extensions for 1099 forms
 If you need additional time to file your 1099 forms, you can request an extension through Form 8809 . Request the extension before the original due date to avoid any late filing penalties.
 Filling out Form 8809 is simpler than filling out a 1099 form .
 Here’s a step-by-step guide to obtaining an extension for filing 1099 forms:
 1. Fill out Form 8809:  Download and complete Form 8809, Application for Extension of Time to File Information Returns. This form allows you to request a 30-day extension for filing your 1099 forms. Ensure you provide all the necessary information, including your name, address, and taxpayer identification number.
 2. Submit Form 8809:  Once you’ve completed Form 8809, you can submit it by mail or electronically. If filing by mail, send the form to the address provided on the form instructions. If filing electronically, you can use the IRS FIRE site  for filing information returns electronically.
 3. Provide necessary information:  Along with the extension request, you must also provide a reason for needing the extension. The IRS will evaluate your request based on this information.
 4. Complete 1099 forms on time:  Remember that even with an extension, you can still provide the necessary 1099 forms to your recipients by Feb. 1, 2027.
 By following these steps and submitting your extension request before the original due date, you can avoid late filing penalties and ensure you have the necessary time to accurately complete your 1099 filings.
 FYI:  Even with an extension, recipients must still receive their necessary 1099 forms by the initial deadline—generally Feb. 1, 2027.
 Tips to avoid missing Form 1099 deadlines
 Missing small business tax form  deadlines can result in penalties and unnecessary stress. You’ll want to create a calendar system to keep you on track.
 To avoid missing a 1099 deadline, here are some best practices to follow:
 1. Keep accurate records:  Keep detailed records of your payments to independent contractors throughout the year. It’ll be easier to compile the necessary information when it’s time to file your 1099 forms.
 2. Know your specific deadlines:  Different types of Form 1099 have different filing deadlines. Be aware of the specific due dates for each form. Familiarize yourself with your deadlines to avoid any last-minute rushes.
 3. Set reminders:  Mark important 1099 deadlines on your calendar or set up automated reminders. This step will help ensure you don’t forget to submit forms on time.
 Missing Form 1099 deadlines can lead to penalties and additional stress during tax season.
 Can you file 1099 forms online?
 Yes, businesses are strongly encouraged to file 1099 forms electronically. The IRS FIRE system accepts e-filed forms, and many accounting platforms let you generate and e-file 1099s directly.
 E-filing not only saves time but also reduces the risk of missed deadlines or lost paperwork.
 Find peace of mind come tax time
 Tax season is stressful for individuals and business owners alike, especially when managing and navigating the 1099 deadline. However, the right strategies can help ensure a smooth tax filing process.
